items.headline: Council agenda listed $3.79M power-modeling software deal for Silicon Valley Power
items.summary: The November 10 City Council agenda listed an action to delegate authority to the City Manager to sign an agreement with cQuant.io, Inc. for generation resource modeling software for Silicon Valley Power. The maximum compensation is $3,791,855 over a ten-year term.

items.headline: Campbell Planning Commission agenda: rezone 480 Chapman from commercial to single-family
items.summary: The November 10 agenda listed a public hearing on a request to change the land use and zoning of 480 Chapman, a single-family home on neighborhood-commercial land, to Low Density Residential and R-1-10. The change would end the home's legal nonconforming status and remove its T4N.M-O form-based designation. Staff recommended that the commission send the request to the City Council with a recommendation to approve, with a tentative council date of December 1, 2026.

items.headline: Campbell planning commissioners work on two permit-streamlining efforts
items.summary: The November 10 agenda listed reports from two ad hoc subcommittees. One, led by Commissioners Buchbinder and Kamkar, plans to interview developers and other stakeholders to find housing production bottlenecks and propose policies. The other, led by Commissioners Zisser and Aquilina, is researching ways to streamline Conditional Use Permits to support business development.

items.headline: 363-apartment Hanover project proposed to replace Stevens Creek offices
items.summary: The Planning Commission's November 10 agenda listed The Hanover Company's 363-unit apartment proposal at 19220-19300 Stevens Creek Boulevard. It would replace existing office buildings on Sites 5 and 6 of the city's Priority Housing Sites and uses SB 330 and State Density Bonus law. The agenda item covered Architectural and Site Approval, a Parcel Map, and a Tree Removal Permit.

items.headline: Preschool for up to 192 kids proposed at 855 E. Homestead Road
items.summary: The Planning Commission's November 9 agenda listed a Special Development Permit to demolish a vacant commercial building on a 1.11-acre office-zoned site. It would be replaced by a 16,000-square-foot, two-story childcare and preschool for up to 192 children, with a new eight-foot masonry wall along the western and part of the southern property lines. The applicant is listed as CASCO of Primrose Schools.

items.headline: Sunnyvale planning commissioners to review rewrite of citywide residential parking rules
items.summary: The November 9 Planning Commission agenda listed a recommendation to the City Council on an ordinance that would repeal and replace the city's parking chapter (19.46). It would also amend parking-related provisions for the Downtown, Lawrence Station and El Camino Real plan districts, and the Dual Urban Opportunity Housing chapter, affecting residential off-street parking requirements citywide.

items.headline: Historic commission agenda: 1,200 sq ft backyard unit at 1391 Washington Street
items.summary: The November 5 agenda listed a public hearing on a recommendation for a 1,200-square-foot detached accessory dwelling unit and a 347-square-foot detached garage at 1391 Washington Street, a property on the city's Historic Resource Inventory. The same agenda had the commission selecting one member for the review board that will choose a consultant for the update of Santa Clara's Historic Preservation Ordinance.

items.headline: Heritage commission agenda included briefing on new SB 9 lot-split changes
items.summary: The November 4 agenda listed a staff presentation on recent changes to SB 9, including SB 450 and AB 1061, which changed requirements for two-unit developments and urban lot splits in single-family zones. The same agenda also listed a possible priority project recommendation to the City Council and approval of a 2027 work plan.
